passage: Tissues are groups of cells that work together to perform a specific function, showing a clear division of labour in multicellular organisms. In plants, growth is not uniform; it is restricted to specific regions called meristematic tissues. While some plant tissues like xylem and phloem are essential for transport, others like sclerenchyma provide structural support even though they consist of dead cells. These dead cells are not waste; they are vital for the plant's strength. In animals, tissues are diverse. Epithelial tissue forms protective coverings not just on the skin, but also lines internal organs and cavities. Connective tissues are equally varied. Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports substances, proving that tissues do not need to be solid to function. Bones are also living connective tissues filled with cells, not dry, inert structures. Furthermore, the body contains involuntary muscles that function automatically without our conscious control. Unlike hollow pipes, nerves are complex structures that transmit electrical impulses to coordinate body activities. Understanding these tissues helps us see how specialized cells maintain life.

items.evidence: These dead cells are not waste; they are vital for the plant's strength.
items.q: Why does a plant keep sclerenchyma, even though its cells are dead?
options: The dead cells give the plant strength
The dead cells store waste for the plant
The dead cells help the plant grow taller
The dead cells carry food to the leaves
items.explain: Dead sclerenchyma cells are not waste; they give the plant strength and structural support.

wrong.why: thinks dead cells are only waste
mixes support with growth, which is meristem work
mixes sclerenchyma with phloem's food transport

items.evidence: In plants, growth is not uniform; it is restricted to specific regions called meristematic tissues.
items.q: A gardener ties a thread around a young stem. Where will new growth mainly happen?
options: In the special growing regions of the stem
Evenly along the whole length of the stem
In every cell that touches another cell
In the dead cells that give strength
items.explain: Plant growth is restricted to meristematic regions, so it is not the same everywhere in the body.

wrong.why: thinks plants grow evenly like animals
thinks any touching cells form a growing tissue
thinks dead cells have no role, yet picks them

items.evidence: Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports substances, proving that tissues do not need to be solid to function.
items.q: Which example shows that a tissue can work without being solid?
options: Blood, which carries substances around the body
Bone, which holds the body upright
Nerves, which carry signals to the brain
Skin covering, which protects the body
items.explain: Blood is a fluid connective tissue that carries substances, so tissues need not be solid.

wrong.why: thinks bone is dry and hard, so picks it as the only tissue type
thinks nerves carry liquid in hollow tubes
thinks epithelium is only the skin surface

items.evidence: Epithelial tissue forms protective coverings not just on the skin, but also lines internal organs and cavities.
items.q: How does epithelial tissue protect an animal body?
options: It covers the skin and lines inner organs
It covers only the skin on the outside
It joins bones to each other inside
It carries impulses to coordinate the body
items.explain: Epithelial tissue covers the skin and also lines internal organs and cavities.

wrong.why: thinks epithelium is only on the outer skin
mixes epithelium with ligaments joining parts
